rendered: The document does not give a clinical sensitivity or specificity for the sepsis serum samples. It reports no such figures and no related diagnostic metrics such as false positives or negatives, predictive values or AUC.[1]What it does report is qualitative. Serum came from septic patients with confirmed E. coli infection, septic patients with confirmed E. faecium infection, and healthy volunteers as controls. Each sample was measured repeatedly, and the points on the LDA score plot are technical replicates. The paper says this plot[2][3] exhibits well-resolved, non-overlapping clusters for the three tested serum groups[4] (see Fig. 5[5], panel c). The conclusion only says the probe successfully distinguished two types of clinical sepsis serum samples[6]. The only percentage accuracy in the paper is a 100% classification accuracy[7], and it belongs to the varying-concentration tests, not the clinical serum samples. Since only replicate measurements of a few serum samples were plotted, sensitivity and specificity could not be worked out from the data shown.
